Proposition
[The tangent space of a regular level set is the kernel of the differential]

↗ prop:regular-level-set-inclusion-smooth ↗ prop:regular-level-set-hypersurface-codim-one

In the situation of Proposition 12, for every $x_0 \in f^{-1}(c)$ the image of $d(\iota _c)_{x_0}$ is exactly $\ker df_{x_0}$; that is, $T_{x_0} f^{-1}(c) = \ker df_{x_0}$ under the usual identification.

Proof

↗ prop:regular-level-set-inclusion-smooth For the inclusion $\subseteq $: the composite $f \circ \iota _c$ is the constant $c$ on $f^{-1}(c)$, so by the chain rule $df_{x_0} \circ d(\iota _c)_{x_0} = 0$, that is, every vector in the image of $d(\iota _c)_{x_0}$ lies in $\ker df_{x_0}$.

For equality, compare dimensions. By Proposition 12 the map $d(\iota _c)_{x_0}$ is injective on the $n$-dimensional space $T_{x_0} f^{-1}(c)$, so its image has dimension $n$. On the other side, $df_{x_0}$ is a nonzero linear functional on the $(n+1)$-dimensional space $T_{x_0}M$, so its kernel has dimension $n$. A subspace of dimension $n$ contained in a subspace of dimension $n$ equals it.

□

Suppose $\bar{M}$ is a smooth manifold and $M \subseteq \bar{M}$ is an embedded codimension-$k$ submanifold. A smooth map $\Phi : \bar{M} \to \mathbb {R}^k$ is called a defining function for $M$ if $M$ is a regular level set of $\Phi $. More generally, if $\Phi : U \to \mathbb {R}^k$ is a smooth map defined on an open subset $U \subseteq \bar{M}$ such that $M \cap U$ is a regular level set of $\Phi $, then $\Phi $ is called a local defining function for $M$. The following is a partial converse to the submersion level set theorem.
